discoveries.headline: What tokenisation actually means, from the world's biggest asset manager
discoveries.why: BlackRock's plain guide explains how a fund, a bond or a building can be recorded as a token on a blockchain, without changing the thing itself. It is honest about the risks too: smart-contract flaws and rules still being written. The foundation for every real-world asset you will hear about.

discoveries.headline: COP31 in seven minutes, for the bus
discoveries.why: ABC's The World Today on the opening days in Antalya, with Australia's Chris Bowen leading the negotiations and a push for a 2035 electrification goal. A quick, clear catch-up on the summit that runs until 20 November.

discoveries.headline: A gorilla stops to admire a butterfly
discoveries.why: In Bwindi, Uganda, Mary Schrader caught a mountain gorilla in a moment of pure curiosity, and it took top honours for animal portraits. Look at the gentleness in the hands, then find one small thing outside worth that much attention.
discoveries.meta_credit: Photograph: Mary Schrader · World Nature Photography Awards
discoveries.credit: “Shared wonder” © Mary Schrader, World Nature Photography Awards 2026, Animal Portraits

discoveries.headline: Arrive in open presence with Tara Brach
discoveries.why: A spacious guided sit from one of the world's best-loved teachers: settle the body, soften the effort, and rest in awareness of whatever is here. Perfect with headphones on the way in.

discoveries.headline: Why some people run out of energy, and how to feel alive again
discoveries.why: TED Radio Hour's Manoush Zomorodi talks with mitochondrial scientist Martin Picard and breath writer James Nestor about stress, breathing and the tiny power plants in your cells. Stress is the blind spot; this is a friendly way in.

discoveries.headline: Chloe Anne wins the 2026 Richell Prize
discoveries.why: The Richell Prize backs unpublished Australian writers on the way to their first book. Read the announcement, then look out for Chloe Anne's name. Championing someone early is how great careers start.

discoveries.headline: Dinacharya: rhythm, not rigidity
discoveries.why: The Ayurvedic daily routine in plain steps: rise early, scrape the tongue, sip warm water, move gently, sit quietly, eat your biggest meal at midday and be in bed by ten. Pick just one to add tomorrow.
discoveries.meta_credit: Lisa Pletzer · Art of Living Retreat Center

discoveries.headline: Ten minutes for your neck, shoulders and upper back
discoveries.why: Adriene's quick practice undoes the hunch from phones, laptops and steering wheels. Do it before you open the inbox.

discoveries.headline: Ten strength moves with a water bottle and a shopping bag
discoveries.why: LiveUp, a government-funded program, shows ten low-impact exercises that build balance, bone and everyday strength at home. Start with one set of each, twice a week.
